sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and no prima-facie case is made out against them.
Applicant no.1 is husband of the opposite party no.2 and that entire family of applicant no.1 has named in the First Information Report and charge-sheet has been submitted in a routine manner.
It is further submitted that impugned summoning order dated 24.12.2018 has been passed on a proforma by merely filling in the date of order.
There is no reference in the impugned summoning order regarding case number, name of accused, sections of offence etc.

It was submitted that impugned summoning order is a cyclostyle order and there is absolutely nothing to show that the concerned Magistrate has applied any judicial mind by passing the impugned summoning order.
4. Learned AGA submits that a prima-facie case is made out against the applicants but it could not be disputed that impugned summoning order has been passed on a printed proforma by filling details of the case.
5.
I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.
6. Perusal of record shows that the impugned cognizance and summoning order dated 24.12.2018 has been passed on a printed proforma and by filling in date of the order.

7. It is apparent from record that impugned cognizance/summoning order is a proforma order and neither the sections of offence nor the names of accused persons have been mentioned in the summoning order.
Even the case number has not been mentioned.
Merely date of order and next date was filled in blank column of proforma.
It is well settled that summoning order has to be passed after considering relevant material and applying judicial mind.
In the instant case, it is apparent that the impugned order has been passed in a mechanical way without applying judicial mind.

8. It may be stated that there are hundreds of decisions of this Court to the effect that the summoning order cannot be passed on a printed proforma by merely filling in the details of the case,
rather the summoning order must be passed by applying judicial mind.
To mention a few cases

,
reference may be made to the case of Ankit Vs. State of U.P. J.I.C. 2010 (1) 432, Basasudin and others Vs. State of U.P. 2011 (1) JIC, 335 All, Abdul Rashid and others Vs. State of U.P. 2010 (3) JIC,

State of U.P. (Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.7972/2022) and Ram Kewal Vs. State of U.P.
2024:AHC-LKO:5736.

sentences.text: It is well-settled that summoning of a person as an accused is a serious matter and thus, the summoning order must reflect of judicial mind.
It is a mater of grave concern that such orders are being passed by some of the Magistrates in such a careless and negligent manner disregarding the position of law.
The practice of passing of summoning orders on printed proforma by merely filling the details of case must be stopped forthwith.

10. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned summoning order dated 24.12.2018, passed by the Civil Judge (S.D.)/Fast Track Court/A.C.J.M., Kanpur Dehat, is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the court concerned to pass the order on cognizance and summoning afresh expeditiously in accordance with law.
11.
